hazard_consequence_node.label: HazardConsequence
hazard_consequence_node.name: Pool fire
hazard_consequence_node.evidence: The incident description repeatedly identifies the event as a pool fire: the Pearland Fire Chief 'observed a ground level pool fire, 65 to 80 feet in width' east of warehouse 1. CSB states that 'the initial small fire involving the smaller containers resulted in a pool fire,' and that ruptured drums, failed blend tanks, and the failed tank wagon added fuel so that burning liquid 'flowed toward the storage tanks and the warehouses.' Section 2.3.4 further describes a 'Liquid Pool Fire at Tank Farm and Warehouses' and explains that inadequate drainage/containment allowed released burning liquids to spread through the facility.
hazard_consequence_node.explanation: The central accident mechanism analyzed in the report is the formation and spread of burning liquid pools from released combustible/flammable liquids. The report focuses on how a small initial fire escalated because drums ruptured, tanks failed, and inadequate containment and drainage allowed the burning liquid pool to spread into the tank farm and warehouses. This makes pool fire the primary hazard consequence.

entity_nodes.label: Material
entity_nodes.name: combustible liquids
entity_nodes.evidence: Approximately 10 drums of combustible liquid were located on and around packaging line 4
entity_nodes.explanation: Combustible liquid products stored in drums and other containers near packaging line 4 were a principal fuel source for the spreading pool fire.

condition_nodes.label: Phase
condition_nodes.name: Liquid
condition_nodes.evidence: the liquid pool fire was also observed to be moving from the warehouse 1 area toward the front of the facility
condition_nodes.explanation: The hazardous material was burning as pooled liquid on the ground.

condition_nodes.label: Pressure
condition_nodes.name: High pressure
condition_nodes.evidence: these drums ruptured due to internal pressure and released their contents
condition_nodes.explanation: Closed containers were heated by fire, building internal pressure before rupture and release.

condition_nodes.label: Temperature
condition_nodes.name: High temperature
condition_nodes.evidence: it was already being heated to a significant temperature
condition_nodes.explanation: Fire exposure raised equipment and liquid temperature enough to cause venting and structural failure.

condition_nodes.label: Combustibility
condition_nodes.name: Combustible
condition_nodes.evidence: containing a combustible liquid synthetic motor oil
condition_nodes.explanation: The released material was capable of burning and sustaining the pool fire.

condition_nodes.label: ReleaseType
condition_nodes.name: Instant release
condition_nodes.evidence: these drums ruptured due to internal pressure and released their contents
condition_nodes.explanation: The drum failures caused sudden loss of liquid contents that rapidly enlarged the burning pool.

event_nodes.label: InitiatingEvent
event_nodes.name: Initial fire starts outside adjacent to warehouse 1
event_nodes.evidence: it is most likely that the fire started outside, directly adjacent to warehouse 1
event_nodes.explanation: The earliest identified abnormal event was an outdoor fire near warehouse 1; the exact cause of that fire was not determined.

event_nodes.label: MechanicalFailure
event_nodes.name: Rupture of drums of combustible liquid at packaging line 4
event_nodes.evidence: these drums ruptured due to internal pressure and released their contents
event_nodes.explanation: Drum rupture was a direct loss-of-containment event that added fuel to the pool fire and accelerated fire spread.
